title: Functorial transported module structure on the etale inverse image
statement: Let $U,V$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], $f:U\to V$ a morphism, and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings on $V_{\mathrm{Et}}$ [def-weil-pbc-etale-site]. Let $L$ be the inverse image on sheaves of sets, $a_S:L\dashv R$ its adjunction, $L_a$ the abelian inverse image and $a:L_a\dashv R_a$ its fixed adjunction, and $R_r$ the sectionwise direct image on ring sheaves [lem-weil-pbc-etale-inverse-image-algebraic-structures]. Write $F_{r,T}$ and $F_{a,T}$ for the forgetful functors to set sheaves on $T=U,V$. Fix a ring inverse-image functor $L_r$, an adjunction $a_r:L_r\dashv R_r$, and natural isomorphisms $e_r:L_rF_{r,U}\cong F_{r,V}L$ and $e_a:L_aF_{a,U}\cong F_{a,V}L$. Assume the two hom-equivalence equations: for every ring map $h:L_rG\to F$, $F_{r,V}(a_r(h))=a_S(e_{r,G}^{-1}\circ F_{r,U}(h))$, and for every abelian map $h:L_aG\to F$, $F_{a,V}(a(h))=a_S(e_{a,G}^{-1}\circ F_{a,U}(h))$. Sheaves of modules and their forgetful functors to abelian sheaves are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Then there exist a functor $L_M:\mathrm{Mod}(\mathcal O)\to\mathrm{Mod}(L_r\mathcal O)$ and a natural isomorphism $e:L_MF_U\cong F_VL_a$ such that the actual scalar action on every $L_MG$ is the transported action. Explicitly, put $i_G=F_{a,U}(e_G)\circ e_{a,F_VG}$. There are set-sheaf morphisms $\mu_V:F_{r,V}\mathcal O\times F_{a,V}F_VG\to F_{a,V}F_VG$ and $\mu_U:F_{r,U}L_r\mathcal O\times F_{a,U}F_UL_MG\to F_{a,U}F_UL_MG$ whose section maps are the actual scalar multiplications, and $L(\mu_V)=i_G\circ\mu_U\circ(e_{r,\mathcal O}^{-1}\times i_G^{-1})\circ\lambda$, where $\lambda:L(X\times Y)\to LX\times LY$ is the canonical product comparison.

proof.text: Choose the objectwise transported modules H and abelian comparisons d from the object theorem.

Apply the proved transported-map linearity theorem and PresheafOfModules.homMk to lift each conjugated abelian map to a module morphism. Faithfulness of SheafOfModules.toSheaf proves the identity and composition laws, giving LM. NatIso.ofComponents assembles d into the natural isomorphism; its naturality follows by canceling d.inv followed by d.hom. The chosen objectwise action equations give the required functorwise action conclusion.
